faq.heading: Common questions
faq.subheading: Everything you need to know before you give.
faq.q1: Is it secure to use Causekind?
faq.a1: Yes, completely secure. We process all payments through verified gateways like Razorpay, and every campaign is verified by our admin team.
faq.q2: How do you check campaigns before they go live?
faq.a2: Every campaign and item request is reviewed by our team before it appears on the site. We verify the person's identity and confirm that the need is genuine. Anything that doesn't pass our checks is rejected.
faq.q3: Can I donate physical items like clothes or books?
faq.a3: Yes. Browse the In-Kind Requests section to find people nearby who need specific items. Once you pick a request, you can arrange to hand over the items directly or through one of our listed drop points.
faq.q4: How does money get to the campaign?
faq.a4: Donations are collected and held securely. Once a campaign reaches its target or its deadline passes, funds are transferred directly to the recipient. You receive a confirmation email at each stage.
faq.q5: Can I track where my donation goes?
faq.a5: Yes. After donating, you can log in to see the status of your donation and get a verified impact certificate once the funds or items are delivered.
faq.q6: Who can post a campaign or request?
faq.a6: Anyone can register as a Donee and submit a campaign or item request. Every submission goes through our approval process before it becomes visible to donors.
faq.a7: Individuals are checked with ID and address. NGOs are checked with their official registration documents. Every request is reviewed by our team before it goes live.
faq.a8: No. Only your area is shown publicly. Handover details are shared only between the donor and the person receiving, once a match is confirmed.
faq.a9: Useful items like books, clothes, furniture, electronics, household and sports items, and more. Used items are welcome. Just describe the condition honestly when you list it, including anything that needs repair.
faq.a10: You meet in person to hand over the item, and confirm it in the app with a one-time code. We recommend meeting in a public place.
faq.q11: What if the handover doesn't happen?
faq.a11: You can cancel, and the need goes back live for other donors.
faq.a13: Yes. It's completely free for donors, donees and NGOs.
faq.a14: Not yet. We're starting with items only. Online donations and fundraising are coming soon.
faq.ngoDriveQ1: How do you verify NGOs and drives?
faq.ngoDriveA1: NGOs are checked with their official registration documents and address. Every drive is reviewed by our team before it goes live to confirm the need is genuine.
faq.ngoDriveQ2: Will my address and contact details be shared?
faq.ngoDriveA2: No. Only your area is shown publicly. Handover details are shared only between you and the NGO once your offer is accepted.
faq.ngoDriveQ3: Can I see the NGO's phone number?
faq.ngoDriveA3: The organization phone is on the NGO's public page. The drive contact person's phone number is shared after the NGO accepts your offer.
faq.ngoDriveQ4: What condition should donated items be in?
faq.ngoDriveA4: Items should match the condition requested on this drive. If marked as working order, items must be fully functional.
faq.ngoDriveA5: You meet in person or arrange drop-off/pickup, and confirm handover in the app with a 6-digit code.

about.headline: Our Mission & Story
about.subheadline: Connecting kind hearts directly with verified needs.
about.visionText: To build a transparent and efficient ecosystem where every act of kindness directly reaches the person in need.
about.missionText: To simplify in-kind donations, eliminate middlemen, and utilize intelligent matching to direct resources where they matter most.
about.storyText: CauseKind began with a simple idea: that charity should be direct, localized, and transparent. We noticed that massive amounts of usable items—books, toys, clothes, and electronics—gather dust in homes, while local organizations and students nearby struggle to acquire them. By integrating a geo-radius matching system, we make sharing seamless and immediate.
about.communityText: Our platform matches you with verified needs within a 10km radius. This localized model completely bypasses courier shipping fees, allowing neighbors to support neighbors directly through safe, approved drop-offs.
about.securePlatformText: We facilitate direct connections under strict administrative moderation and location matching.
about.verifiedNeedsText: Our team reviews every listing and request manually. Safe, verified, direct support.
about.ctaText: Register as a Donor to start listing spare supplies and help verified needs in your community, or sign up as a Donee to seek support for your educational, medical, or family causes.

giveSafely.heading: How to check a charity before you hand anything over.
giveSafely.standfirst: Most giving goes exactly where it should. The checks below are for the small share that does not, and none of them take more than a few minutes. They apply wherever you give — including somewhere that is not us.

registration.title: Ask for the registration
registration.body: A legitimate organisation gives you its registration number without being pressed, and does not treat the question as an insult.

destination.title: Ask where this item goes
destination.body: Which programme, which people, roughly when. A specific answer is a good sign; a vague one is worth pausing on.

proof.title: Get proof it arrived
proof.body: Not proof you sent it — proof it was received, ideally something you did not write yourself.

urgency.title: Be wary of urgency
urgency.body: Pressure to decide immediately is common in donation scams and rare in real need, which is usually patient because it is ongoing.

Faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
Faq.q1: Why can an application be sent back?
Faq.a1: Applications are sent back if uploaded documents are blurry, expired, or if details don't match the registered NGO name. You will receive specific feedback on what needs to be fixed.
Faq.a2: Our team manually reviews every application to ensure authenticity. You will be notified via email once the review is complete.
Faq.q3: What items can I ask for?
Faq.a3: You can request physical goods like blankets, books, medical supplies, food packets, etc. CauseKind does not facilitate direct monetary donations for drives.

nm.title: Legal name
nm.text: Your full name exactly as it is on your Aadhaar, PAN or passport. We match it with the ID you upload.

age.title: Age
age.text: Your age in years. It comes from your profile — update the profile if it's wrong.

ad.title: Current address
ad.text: Where you live now. If it's different from your ID, we may ask for a recent bill or rent agreement.

em.title: Email
em.text: We send review updates here. It's never shown to donors.

ph.title: Phone
ph.text: A number we can call about this application. It's never shown publicly.

forWhom.title: Who the fundraiser is for
forWhom.text: Choose “Me” if the money is for you. Choose “Someone else” if you're raising it for a family member or someone you help.

bn.title: Their full legal name
bn.text: The person's name exactly as on their ID. Only CauseKind reviewers see it — never donors.

pn.title: Name shown to donors
pn.text: What donors will see, e.g. “Ramesh” or “Ramesh K.”. A first name is fine if they want privacy.

ag.title: Their age
ag.text: Pick the age group they fall in. Fundraisers for children may need extra checks.

rl.title: Your relationship
rl.text: How you know them — parent, spouse, guardian and so on.

au.title: Why you
au.text: In a few lines, why you're the right person to raise money for them. For example: “I'm her son and I'm handling the hospital bills.”

cat.title: What is the money for?
cat.text: Pick the one closest to your need. It tells us which papers to ask you for.

wh.title: What happened
wh.text: Tell us what happened and what the money will pay for, in your own words. Only our team reads this.

ur.title: Date
ur.text: The day you need the money by. For example, the day of the operation or the last day to pay fees.

rq.title: Related item request
rq.text: Only if you also asked for items (not money) on CauseKind for the same need. Enter that request number. Otherwise leave it blank.

costs.title: What the money pays for
costs.text: You can skip this, but it helps. Write each thing, how much it costs, and the number on its bill. Example: “Operation ₹80,000 · Bill 4512”.

help.title: Money you already have
help.text: Money you have now, or will get from somewhere else. Our team looks at it, but it is not taken away from the total. Write 0 if none.

insuranceAmount.title: From insurance
insuranceAmount.text: How much your insurance will pay. Write 0 if none.

ownContribution.title: From you or your family
ownContribution.text: How much you or your family can pay. Write 0 if none.

grantsAmount.title: From schemes or grants
grantsAmount.text: Money from a government scheme, scholarship or trust. Write 0 if none.

otherFundraisingAmount.title: From other fundraising
otherFundraisingAmount.text: Money collected somewhere else, like another website, your workplace or your community. Write 0 if none.

ask.title: How much money
ask.text: The total money you need. If you list costs below, it should be the same as “Still needed” — if not, tell us why.

ev_ORGANISER_ID.title: Your identity
ev_ORGANISER_ID.text: A clear photo or PDF of your Aadhaar, PAN, passport or voter ID. Never shown publicly.

ev_ADDRESS_PROOF.title: Address proof
ev_ADDRESS_PROOF.text: A recent electricity bill, rent agreement or bank statement with your current address. Never shown publicly.

ev_MEDICAL_REPORT.title: Medical report
ev_MEDICAL_REPORT.text: The doctor's report or note about this condition. Just this condition — not your whole medical history.

ev_TREATMENT_ESTIMATE.title: Treatment estimate
ev_TREATMENT_ESTIMATE.text: The hospital's written estimate or quote showing the costs you listed.

ev_ENROLMENT_PROOF.title: Enrolment proof
ev_ENROLMENT_PROOF.text: Your admission letter or ID card showing the institution and course.

ev_FEE_STATEMENT.title: Fee statement
ev_FEE_STATEMENT.text: The fee receipt or demand from the institution showing the amount and period.

ev_EVENT_EVIDENCE.title: What happened
ev_EVENT_EVIDENCE.text: An official record of the event: an FIR or police report (theft, accident), a fire brigade report or panchnama (fire), a tehsildar or disaster relief certificate (flood), or a death certificate (loss of an earning member).

ev_CONSENT.title: Consent
ev_CONSENT.text: A signed note from the person you're raising for, saying they agree to this fundraiser.

ev_OTHER.title: Anything else
ev_OTHER.text: Optional. Anything that helps explain the need. It won't speed up the review.

t.title: Campaign title
t.text: A short, plain headline donors see first. Say who and what, e.g. “Help Ramesh walk again after hip surgery”.

cCat.title: Category
cCat.text: Fixed from your approved application. It can't be changed here.

dn.title: Name shown to donors
dn.text: The beneficiary's name on the public page. Use a first name if they want privacy.

cv.title: Cover photo
cv.text: The main picture on your page. Use a clear photo you have permission to share. Avoid showing IDs, bills or other people's faces without consent.

alt.title: Photo description
alt.text: Optional. One sentence describing the photo for people using screen readers, e.g. “Ramesh smiling in a hospital bed”.

st.title: Your story
st.text: Tell donors who needs help, what happened, what the money covers and what difference it makes. Keep it honest — no phone numbers or addresses.

ccb.title: Cost breakdown
ccb.text: What donors see about where the money goes. Changes from your approved application need a reason.

why.title: Reason for the change
why.text: Why the amount or costs differ from what was approved, e.g. “The hospital revised its quote”.

tg.title: Target
tg.text: The total you want to raise on this page. It should match your approved amount unless you give a reason.

ed.title: End date
ed.text: The last day people can donate. Donations stop automatically after this date.

vis.title: Names and place
vis.text: Choose how much donors see: full name, first name only, or hidden — and whether to show your city or state.

pe.title: Documents donors can see
pe.text: Optional. Pick documents that build trust, like a hospital estimate. Your ID and address proof can never be shown.

pChanges.title: What to change
pChanges.text: List exactly what the organiser must fix before you can publish, e.g. “Remove the hospital file number from the story.” They see this.

pDecline.title: Reason
pDecline.text: Why this page can't be published. The organiser sees it — be clear and kind.

pMessage.title: Message to the organiser
pMessage.text: Optional. A short note they see with the approval, e.g. “Looks good — thank you.”

ref.title: Bill or receipt number
ref.text: The number printed on the bill, receipt or price paper for this thing. It helps us check your papers.

ev_RELATIONSHIP_PROOF.title: Proof of relationship
ev_RELATIONSHIP_PROOF.text: Shows how you are related to the person you're raising for: a ration card, birth certificate, or IDs with the same family name or address.

ev_COST_PROOF.title: Cost proof
ev_COST_PROOF.text: A quotation, estimate or bill for what the money will pay for, so reviewers can check the amount.

ev_supporting.title: Supporting document
ev_supporting.text: One more document that shows the need is real, such as an official letter or a report of what happened. It must be a separate upload from your cost proof.
